chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sa'd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

We were with him eight men, and we mentioned Ramadan. He said: Do not say: 'This is Ramadan,' nor 'Ramadan has gone,' nor 'Ramadan has come.' Indeed, Ramadan is a Name from the Names of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. It does not come, nor does it go away, but it is only that which is perishable that comes and goes. However, say: 'The Month of Ramadan.' For the month added to the Name, and the Name is the Name of Allah, and that is the month in which the Qur'an was sent down, which Allah, Exalted is He, made as a sign and a warning.

key_terms.رَمَضَانُ: Ramadan, identified here as a divine Name
key_terms.شَهْرُ مَضَانَ: The Month of Ramadan (distinguishing the month from the Name)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of saying 'Ramadan is a Name of Allah' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the theological nuance of referring to Ramadan as a 'Name of Allah,' distinguishing the eternal divine attribute from the transient temporal month. This linguistic precision, preserved in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, underscores the sanctity of the month by linking it directly to the revelation of the Qur'an, thereby elevating it from a mere calendar period to a sacred manifestation of divine grace.
